svg.title: How a tracking radar is designed from open physics: open sources into an ontology, skills and tools generated from it, an agent that proposes and a simulator that scores one scenario at a time, a test lab that measures the loop, and a workbench where people decide and their decisions go back into the ontology

ceiling: exhaustive search · floor: the textbook S-band tracker
194 planted errors — caught 0.995, per kind
Stone Soup agrees on the tracker, 24 cases, to machine precision
held-out model numbers: not run, so not quoted
a vendor brochure is a claim, never a score

g.style: offset-path:path('M 978.0 670.0 L 891.0 713.5 L 873.0 704.5');offset-rotate:0deg;offset-distance:100%;opacity:1;transition:offset-distance 2s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) 300ms, opacity .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1);animation:iso-in .4s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) 300ms both
g.text: proposals, with their run, checks, models and cost
a reviewer — the burst was the right lever. Accept.
a reviewer — this RCS prior is too optimistic here →
a change request, with this scenario as the evidence
the chair — a vendor number is a claim, never a parameter;
the workbench is designed; the team has not yet sat
a receipt per scenario · never the same person twice
accepted change requests → the physicist, at the library
ontology release 1.1.0 — the decisions, now data
skills regenerated
named codes reloaded · checker regenerated
measured on the same held-out set before it counts
the next scenario — under the new release
SCENE 13 OF 14
People are activated: the workbench
the design store → the reviewers · the chair
proposals with their evidence → receipts per scenario (accept · edit ·
reject) · "the simulator is too harsh here" → a change request with
evidence
